name: Emerge Mail – SMTP, Newsletters & Email Marketing
author: Redigit

sections.description:
Your WordPress email, delivered — and your newsletters, done.

Emerge Mail connects your site to Emerge, the email platform that sends through the email accounts you already own. Password resets, WooCommerce receipts and form notifications land in the inbox, and newsletters to your own contacts go out from your own address — no shared sending servers, no per-contact pricing.

Connect a free Emerge account in about a minute and you’re sending: up to 300 emails a day, free. Paid plans raise the limits when you grow.

Email that arrives

WordPress’s built-in mail is often flagged as spam or never arrives. Emerge Mail sends every email your site writes through a real mailbox or email provider — Gmail, Microsoft 365, Amazon SES, SMTP, SendGrid, Mailgun, Brevo, Postmark, Resend, Mailjet, ZeptoMail or Zoho Mail — so it carries your domain’s own authentication and reputation.

  • Works with everything. WooCommerce, Contact Form 7, WPForms, membership plugins — anything that sends email just works.
  • Never lose an email. If Emerge can’t send something, WordPress’s own mail delivers it instead.
  • Bounces handled for you. Bounces and spam complaints come back to your site automatically, from every sender, Gmail included.
  • Private by default. Your site’s own email is never tracked.

Newsletters and campaigns, built in

Turn on Newsletters & campaigns and grow an audience from the people already on your site.

  • Contacts from your site — users, commenters, WooCommerce and Easy Digital Downloads customers, and form plugins like Contact Form 7, Gravity Forms and MailPoet.
  • Design in the block editor — write emails the way you write posts, with merge tags and your latest posts pulled in.
  • One-time and recurring campaigns — send now, schedule for later, or set a weekly or monthly newsletter.
  • Live results — see each campaign go out, with opens, clicks and bounces as they happen.
  • Automations — email your list when you publish a post, or welcome every new user.
  • Subscribe forms — a block, shortcode or widget, with double opt-in.

Quieter inbox for you

Stop the WordPress notifications you don’t need — comment moderation, auto-update notices and more. Each one you switch off is kept in the Activity Log instead, with or without an Emerge account.

Built for developers too

Every bounce fires the emerge_mail_bounce_received action, and an X-Emerge-Mail-Ref header on a send comes back with it as client_ref — so your own code can act on undeliverable addresses.

External services

Emerge Mail works with Emerge (app.emerge-email.com), the email platform run by the plugin’s author. Nothing is sent anywhere until you click Connect Emerge.

Connecting is a one-time, secure sign-in: you approve the connection in Emerge, and your site receives its own access key, stored encrypted. After that your site talks to Emerge over its secure API to:

  • send your site’s email — recipients, subject, content and attachments — through your Emerge senders;
  • show your plan, usage and senders, and bring back bounces, complaints and unsubscribes;
  • if you turn on Newsletters & campaigns, keep your contacts (email address, name, subscription status and where they came from) in sync, and send and report on your campaigns, automations and subscribe-form signups.

When you connect, Emerge also receives your site’s address and name and the admin email address. Disconnecting revokes the key, and nothing more is sent. Emerge handles this data as your processor: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.

If a mailbox is connected directly on your site rather than through Emerge, email for it goes straight to that provider — Google, Microsoft, SendGrid, Mailgun, Amazon SES, Brevo or your SMTP server — under that provider’s terms; Google and Microsoft sign-ins go through Emerge’s sign-in service, which keeps nothing (terms, privacy).
sections.installation:
1. Install Emerge Mail from the Plugins screen and activate it.
  2. Open Emerge Mail in your admin sidebar and click Connect Emerge.
  3. Sign in to Emerge, or create a free account, and approve the connection.
  4. Add a sender in Emerge — your Gmail, Microsoft 365, SES, SMTP or email-provider account.
  5. Back in WordPress, send yourself a test from the Senders screen. That’s it — your site’s email now goes through Emerge.

Want newsletters? Turn on Newsletters & campaigns under Emerge Mail → Settings.
sections.faq:
Do I need an Emerge account?

Yes, to send — it’s free for up to 300 emails a day. Without one, the plugin leaves your site’s email as it is, and admin-notification suppression and the Activity Log still work.

Does Emerge send from its own servers?

No. Emerge sends through the accounts you connect to it, so your email comes from your own address and keeps your domain’s reputation.

What happens when I reach my daily limit?

Your site’s email falls back to WordPress’s own mail, so password resets and receipts still go out. Campaign emails wait and send when there’s room.

Why does a campaign say “Sending” after I’ve sent it?

Emerge sends campaigns gradually, at your workspace’s sending speed, which keeps your sending accounts in good standing. The campaign screen shows how far it’s got, and you can pause or resume it any time.

Where do I see who opened or clicked?

Each campaign shows its totals in WordPress, and every number links to the full list of recipients in Emerge.

Can I customize the From name and Reply-To?

Yes, under Emerge Mail → Senders → Sender settings. The From address is your Emerge sender’s.

Can I stop using Emerge later?

Any time. Disconnect and WordPress’s own mail takes over. You can export your contacts from Emerge, and your templates and campaigns stay in WordPress.

What’s removed when I delete the plugin?

Deleting Emerge Mail removes its settings, its connection to Emerge, the Activity Log and its campaign data. Your email templates are WordPress posts and stay. Disconnect first if you also want the site removed from your Emerge account.
sections.changelog:
2.2.0

  • Changed: connecting to Emerge uses Emerge Connect, the same secure sign-in every Emerge integration uses. Sites already connected stay connected.
  • Changed: cancelling on Emerge’s approval screen brings you back with a clear message.
  • Changed: the Activity Log drops its Mailbox and From columns — your Emerge senders and their delivery details are in Emerge.
  • Removed: the site’s own bounce webhook (for providers and the Gmail bounce script set up before Emerge). Emerge reports bounces and complaints of the email it sends, and they still show in the Activity Log.

2.1.0

  • New: campaigns show their real progress from Emerge — sending, paused (and why) or sent — with live counts of sent, waiting, opened, clicked and bounced, on the campaign screen, the Campaigns list, newsletter issues and the Dashboard widget.
  • New: pause and resume a campaign while Emerge is sending it.
  • New: campaigns, automations and contacts link straight to their pages in Emerge for every recipient’s details; automations show what they’ve sent.
  • Changed: the Contacts screen is a summary of your audience by status and segment.
  • Changed: the plugin uses Emerge’s public API for everything it does.
  • Changed: newly supported senders — Postmark, Resend, Mailjet, ZeptoMail and Zoho Mail.
  • Changed: simpler readme, settings and notices.

2.0.0

  • New: send your site’s email and newsletters through a free Emerge account, with bounce handling and newsletters & campaigns built in.
